source_refs.note: Topic 11.7.1 (Structure of Alkenes) with Figures 11.8 to 11.10, printed pages 256-257.

blocks.text: Ethene, C2H4, is the simplest alkene. Each carbon atom in ethene is sp2 hybridised and forms three equivalent sp2 hybrid orbitals lying in the same plane; the unhybridised p orbital lies perpendicular (90 degrees) to the plane of the hybrid orbitals (Figure 11.8). The sp2 orbitals are formed by mixing the 2s orbital with two 2p orbitals, leaving one unhybridised p orbital. In ethene each carbon uses two sp2 orbitals to form two C-H bonds, and the remaining sp2 orbital on each carbon forms the carbon-carbon sigma bond by linear overlap (Figure 11.9). The unhybridised p orbitals of the two carbons, parallel to each other, overlap laterally to form another carbon-carbon bond, the pi bond.

blocks.alt: Orbital drawing on x, y and z axes. Three orange sp2 lobes lie in the xy plane, one along x; two green lobes of the unhybrid p orbital point up and down along z. Labels: Unhybrid p orbital, Hybrid sp2, The set of orbitals sp2 + p.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.8: sp2 hybrid and unhybrid orbitals of C (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.8).

blocks.alt: Two carbons each with a vertical 2pz orbital (lobes above and below) joined by lines labelled pi-bond above and below. Between the carbons two sp2 lobes overlap end to end (sigma-bond). Each carbon has two more sp2 lobes overlapping the 1s orbitals of green H atoms (sigma-bonds).
blocks.caption: Figure 11.9: Bond formation of carbons in ethene (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.9).

blocks.text: The two carbon atoms of the double bond and the four atoms attached directly to them lie in the same plane. The sp2 hybridisation gives a trigonal planar arrangement around each carbon with bond angles of approximately 120 degrees, so ethene is a planar molecule (Figure 11.10).

blocks.alt: Ethene: two C atoms joined by a double bond, with curved lines above and below the double bond for the pi electron cloud; each C carries two green H atoms; a red double-headed arc between the two H atoms on the left carbon is marked 120 degrees.
blocks.caption: Figure 11.10: Structure of ethene (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 11.10).
